title: Session-weighted per-token soft-minimum pilot (directional IO, grace decay)
creator: Maya Singh
description: Run a controlled pilot to validate a session-weighted per-token billing model that charges asymmetric input/output rates but protects small/irregular users with a soft minimum credit and a grace-decay mechanism. The goal is to discover a pricing configuration that (1) reduces billing noise for low-volume interactive sessions, (2) preserves unit economics for high-throughput batch customers, and (3) simplifies enterprise conversations around directional IO without increasing invoice disputes.
background: Customers and sales have flagged two recurring issues: confusion over input vs output billing when sessions mix short inputs with long generated outputs, and churn from small customers who hit a sudden minimum in a growth spike. We already track directional token flows in telemetry; this experiment couples a session-level floor (soft minimum) that can be decayed across subsequent sessions (grace-decay) with adjusted per-token multipliers for ingress/egress. Engineering has prepared a feature flag in the billing service and Console needs a small UX for invoice previews.
proposal_summary: Introduce three treatment arms: (A) Control: current symmetrical per-token pricing; (B) Directional multipliers: input_rate=0.6x, output_rate=1.4x (no minimum); (C) Directional + soft-minimum: same multipliers + session soft-minimum credit of $0.50 per session that decays by 50% after 3 sessions (grace-decay). Pilot duration: 6 weeks, initially 5% of traffic (split across treatment arms), then 20% if metrics look healthy.
experiment_design: Cohorts: Random sampling at the account (billing customer) level. Canary: 5% of eligible hosted-api accounts, exclude enterprise committed accounts and customers with open billing disputes. Metrics collection window: per-session, per-account 30d rolling. Implementation: feature flag in billing API, invoice preview flag in Console. Rollout plan: canary -> 20% -> 50% -> full (subject to guardrails). Failure modes: revenue regression > 3% weekly, invoices disputed > 2% of pilot cohort.
success_metrics: Net revenue delta (MRR) vs control: target neutral or positive
Churn rate delta for small customers (monthly < $50 spend): target reduction or unchanged
Invoice disputes (support tickets referencing charges) in cohort: <= 1.5%
Average effective cost per 1M tokens (ingress/egress): within +/-5% of forecasted model
No measurable increase in tail latency or billing pipeline errors
